skills.name: create_contract
skills.description: Creates a contract template (master data) from explicit values the user provided. NEVER derive hours from contract-type words like 'Vollzeit' — always ask the user for the real values. Use when the user wants to create a new record. parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Contract template name (e.g. 'Standard 80%')

parameters.name: guaranteedHours
parameters.description: Guaranteed hours per payment interval for a fixed-hours contract (path 1). Omit entirely for a contract that inherits the company-wide workload (path 2) — never invent a value.

parameters.name: validFrom
parameters.description: Validity start date (YYYY-MM-DD)

parameters.name: minimumHours
parameters.description: Optional, only meaningful together with guaranteedHours (path 1); defaults to guaranteedHours when set, otherwise stays unconfigured (0)

parameters.name: maximumHours
parameters.description: Optional, only meaningful together with guaranteedHours (path 1); defaults to guaranteedHours when set, otherwise stays unconfigured (0)

parameters.name: fullTime
parameters.description: Optional full-time reference hours for path 1; 0 = not configured. Not meaningful when guaranteedHours is omitted (path 2)

parameters.name: nightRate
parameters.description: Optional night time-credit factor (0.1 = 6 minutes credit per night hour, not money). Omit to keep the standard (scheduling rule, then installation settings); 0 means explicitly no credit.

parameters.name: holidayRate
parameters.description: Optional holiday time-credit factor. Omit to keep the standard (scheduling rule, then installation settings); 0 means explicitly no credit.

parameters.name: saRate
parameters.description: Optional Saturday time-credit factor. Omit to keep the standard (scheduling rule, then installation settings); 0 means explicitly no credit.

parameters.name: soRate
parameters.description: Optional Sunday time-credit factor. Omit to keep the standard (scheduling rule, then installation settings); 0 means explicitly no credit.

parameters.name: performsShiftWork
parameters.description: Optional: whether the employee works late/night shifts. Omit to keep the standard (scheduling rule, then installation default). When false, the contract rates are ignored and the standard rates apply.

parameters.name: paymentInterval
parameters.description: Payment interval; defaults to Monthly

parameters.name: percent
parameters.description: Optional workload share in percent for path 2 (inherited workload); scales the company-wide monthly value and feeds absence macros. Defaults to 100 when omitted — a missing percent is normal, not an error

parameters.name: validUntil
parameters.description: Optional validity end date (YYYY-MM-DD); omit for open-ended

skills.name: partition_clients_by_address
skills.description: Builds the location group tree from client addresses: region → state/province → city cluster for employees, external employees and customers. Centres are cities with enough addresses; every other place joins its nearest centre as a whole, so single addresses need no coordinates. Level 'cluster_municipality' adds municipality sub-groups (Gemeinden). Use for 'create groups from all addresses' or when orders cannot be sealed because no groups exist. Existing groups are reused.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: Granularity: 'cluster' (default) nests density-based city clusters under state groups; 'cluster_municipality' adds municipality sub-groups inside every city cluster (choose it when the user asks for municipalities, Gemeinden, communes or comuni); 'state' one group per state/province; 'city' one flat group per city; 'state_city' every city under its state.

parameters.name: entityType
parameters.description: Client types to place into the tree; 'All' (default) covers employees, external employees and customers together.

parameters.name: clusterSharePercent
parameters.description: Only at levels 'cluster' and 'cluster_municipality': minimum share (1-100) of a state's addresses a city needs to become its own cluster group; defaults to 10. The largest city of every state is always a cluster.

parameters.name: subClusterSharePercent
parameters.description: Only at level 'cluster_municipality': minimum share (1-100) of a city cluster's addresses a place outside the centre city needs to become its own municipality sub-group; it also needs at least 3 addresses. Defaults to 15. Smaller places join the nearest sub-group when it is nearer than the cluster centre, otherwise they stay in the city cluster group, like the residents of the centre city.

parameters.name: rootGroupName
parameters.description: Optional name of an existing group every top-level node attaches under; when omitted, states nest under the regions defined for their country (none: states at the root).

parameters.name: includeAlreadyGrouped
parameters.description: When true, clients that already belong to a group are placed again too; defaults to false so only ungrouped clients get new memberships. The clusters are still computed from ALL addresses, so a re-run lands in the groups of the first run, which are reused by name under the right parent.

parameters.name: validFrom
parameters.description: Start date of the new memberships (format YYYY-MM-DD, 'today', or 'entry' to start each person on their own employment entry date and to pull forward existing memberships of the target group that start later (the preview shows how many)); defaults to today when this is left out. The preview states the consequence for persons who joined earlier, so pass the date or 'entry' the user chose.

parameters.name: apply
parameters.description: When false (default) only previews the plan; when true creates the groups and persists the memberships. Only set true after the user explicitly confirmed the preview.

skills.name: schedule_recurring_task
skills.description: Create or update a recurring (cron) task that Klacksy runs automatically on a schedule for the current user. Use this whenever the user wants something to happen repeatedly at fixed times: a recurring reminder, or a skill that should run periodically. YOU must translate the user's natural-language schedule into a standard 5-field cron expression and pass it as cronExpression.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Short human-readable label for the task, unique per user. Re-using an existing name updates that task.

parameters.name: cronExpression
parameters.description: Standard 5-field cron expression (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week) that YOU derive from the user's natural-language schedule. Examples: '0 8 * * 1' = Mondays 08:00; '0 18 * * *' = every day 18:00; '0 9 1 * *' = 1st of month 09:00; '*/30 * * * *' = every 30 minutes.

parameters.name: actionType
parameters.description: What the task does: 'reminder' delivers messageText, 'skill' runs skillName.

parameters.name: messageText
parameters.description: The reminder text delivered to the user. Required when actionType is 'reminder'.

parameters.name: skillName
parameters.description: The name of the skill to run on the schedule. Required when actionType is 'skill'. Must be an existing, non-sensitive skill.

parameters.name: skillParameters
parameters.description: Optional JSON object of parameters for the scheduled skill, e.g. {"groupId":"..."}.

parameters.name: timeZoneId
parameters.description: Optional IANA time zone the schedule is interpreted in. LEAVE EMPTY unless the user explicitly names a different time zone; when empty the schedule uses the organization's configured time zone (from the app owner's address country). Only set this (e.g. 'America/New_York') when the user explicitly asks for another zone.

parameters.name: maxRuns
parameters.description: Optional maximum number of times the task may run before it disables itself. Leave empty for unlimited.

parameters.name: allowIrreversibleUnattended
parameters.description: Opt-in that lets an IRREVERSIBLE skill run unattended on this one schedule. A new task defaults to false, which makes a background run of such a skill refuse and PAUSE the task instead of executing it. Omitting it when updating an existing task KEEPS that task's current setting. Only set true when the user explicitly accepts that the scheduled skill changes data nobody will confirm at fire time.

parameters.name: apply
parameters.description: When false (default) returns a preview with the next run for confirmation; when true the task is saved.

Also covers the manual/handbook tab with the sample XML download. Use this when the user asks how to set up or use the ERP order import. Supports a level parameter: short (purpose only), elements (every card explained), effects (data flow, how orders become shifts, how tokens and the drop-zone relate).

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: Explanation depth, chosen by the KIND of question (not by the user's experience): 'short' = what is X / what does X mean / why does X exist (purpose only); 'elements' = how do I ... Only an explicit request for the short version or for every step overrides this. Omit for the full document.

skills.name: bundle_nearby_timerange_shifts_into_container
skills.description: Finds all TimeRange task shifts (IsTimeRange=true) that fit a given day's time budget around a city/town/location, creates a brand-new container shift for exactly one weekday, and fills its weekday template with the found tasks in route-optimized order — container creation, autofill and template persistence happen atomically in one transaction with a self-verifying re-read.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: City, town or address used as the route's start and end base (StartBase/EndBase) for finding and ordering nearby TimeRange task shifts.

parameters.name: weekday
parameters.description: ISO weekday (1=Monday..7=Sunday) the new container's weekday template is built for. Exactly one weekday per call.

parameters.name: fromTime
parameters.description: Start of the day's time budget in HH:mm format (e.g. '07:00').

parameters.name: untilTime
parameters.description: End of the day's time budget in HH:mm format (e.g. '18:00').

parameters.name: fromDate
parameters.description: Start date of the new container order's validity in YYYY-MM-DD format. REQUIRED — always ask the user, never silently assume today.

parameters.name: untilDate
parameters.description: Optional end date of the container order's validity in YYYY-MM-DD format. Leave empty for an ongoing/unlimited container. Must be >= fromDate.

parameters.name: transportMode
parameters.description: Transport mode used for route optimization between the found tasks. Without a configured OpenRouteService API key, only 'car' works — 'bicycle', 'foot' and 'mix' are rejected with a clear error instead of silently using a worse fallback route.

parameters.name: timeRangeTolerance
parameters.description: How strictly each task's own TimeRange window is enforced on its planned arrival (0.0-1.0): 1.0 = strict, the arrival must lie inside the window; lower values widen the window on both sides by (1 - value) times its length; 0 disables the check. Defaults to 0.5, the same default used by the UI container autofill.

parameters.name: groupIds
parameters.description: Optional comma-separated list of group IDs (GUIDs) to restrict candidate task shifts to. Use list_groups to resolve names to IDs. Leave empty to consider all matching TimeRange tasks regardless of group.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Optional name of the new container shift. Defaults to 'Mobile Dienste ' followed by the location when omitted, so no extra question is needed.

skills.name: explain_klacksy_personality

skills.name: explain_klacksy_learning

A ready group becomes a learned phrasing, capability, or open wish; useless ones are withdrawn. This runs automatically; an administrator supervises via the 'Klacksy learns' card and gets a weekly digest. Only a 120-character excerpt of a wording is stored. Learning never changes what a capability may do. Use when asked whether Klacksy learns or improves.

Also covers the default and allowed length of its validity. Use this when asked what a token can do or how long it lasts.

parameters.name: expenses
parameters.description: Optional. 'description:amount' or 'description:amount:taxable', several separated by ';'.

parameters.name: noExpenses
parameters.description: Optional. 'this' when the targeted orders have no expenses, 'all' when no order left in the review has any.

parameters.name: acceptProposals
parameters.description: Optional. true takes the proposed start, split, group and qualifications where still undecided.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: Optional. true leaves the targeted orders out of this review.

skills.description: Carries out the confirmed part of the walk-through of the open orders: writes the decided start time, staffing group, required qualifications and expenses to each order, seals it into its plannable shift and cuts it into the decided services, every service carrying the expenses. Runs only after the planner confirmed the shown preview; at most 25 orders per confirmation.
